craft_notes: Sthāyin: the refuge-cry — bidden āśraya. Sanskrit-first: samāśrayata kept imperative (take-refuge, 2nd pl.); anuttarātma kept the vocative-address (O Unsurpassable-self — row 7); sāra kept essence. Rows: 7 (vocative closes the address mid-verse), 1 ('O Unsurpassable-self' lands the addressee last), 12 (the plea settles). Close: 'O Unsurpassable-self.' Rejected: dropping the vocative — killed: the address is the verse's heat; 'scripture'→'canon' — killed: śāstra kept.

lines: Being, take refuge in the scripture —

reads_against.argmap: Whose refuge is the scripture? → The being is bidden to āśraya the śāstra whose sāra is the all-made vimarśa-nature — addressed to the anuttarātman.
c1_essence: Being, take refuge in the scripture whose sāra is the all-made vimarśa — O Unsurpassable-self.
reads_against.c1_rasa: adbhuta-śānta of authority established (wonder settling into doctrinal calm)
